title: Home practical guide and safety card: stair-climb power
subject: Science (GCSE Biology, Chemistry, Physics)
source: Written for gcse-science/y10 lesson 71 (Home practical guide and safety card: stair-climb power (portal worksheet))
intro: Lesson 71: Power. A practical to do at home with an adult nearby. Read it all first.

practical.aim: To estimate your power when climbing stairs
equipment: A flight of stairs at home
safety: Walk, never run; hold the handrail
An adult knows what you are doing and is nearby
Clear a space and tidy up afterwards; wash your hands
method: Measure the height of one step and count the steps; height of the flight = step height × number of steps (in m)
Walk (do not run) up the stairs while your helper times you
Repeat twice more and find the mean time
Work out the work done: weight (mass × 10 N/kg) × height
Power = work done ÷ time, in watts

questions.q: Big question: walker or runner, who has more power?
questions.a: Same work; the runner has more power (less time).
